svg.aria-label: Four ways two threads can use one cache line. 1, true sharing: both threads use one variable and take turns; the line moves on every write and each write waits for the last, so the transfers happen one after another. 2, false sharing: each thread writes its own variable, but both are in one line; writes wait in each core's store buffer and commit in batches, so the line moves now and then. 3, false sharing with a fence or an atomic: each write must own the line before the next can start, so the line moves for nearly every write. 4, padded: each variable on its own line; nothing moves.

g.text: Four ways two threads can use one cache line
Thread A (blue) and thread B (orange) run on different cores. Each block on a timeline is one write.
Both threads use one variable and take turns. Each write waits
for the other thread's, so every transfer is paid in full, in turn.
Each thread writes only its own variable. Writes wait in the core's
store buffer and go in batches whenever it holds the line.
A fence or an atomic makes each write own the line before the
next can start, so the line moves for nearly every write.
Each variable on its own line: each core keeps its line, and
nothing moves. This is what an update costs with no sharing.
